title: Kernel-aware prompt preprocessor with microcache bypass heuristics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The prefill path currently incurs variable CPU overhead for short prompts and heavy prefix reuse due to indiscriminate microcache lookups and generic normalization kernels. This manifests as tail latency spikes and higher per-request CPU while the runtime is scheduling kernels optimized for long sequences. Goal: Implement a small, kernel-aware shim in the prefill pipeline that uses cheap heuristics to decide whether to: 1) serve from an ultra-fast microcache bypass path (minimal normalization + ASCII fastpath), 2) route through lightweight vectorized normalization kernels, or 3) fall back to the existing full tokenizer/normalizer. The shim should be aware of the downstream kernel selection hints (expected decode kernel, kv-cache reuse score, and batchability) so it optimizes for overall GPU/CPU balance rather than pure CPU latency. This ticket covers design, instrumentation, implementation of the shim, and rollout gating with perf/regression checks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Shim inserted into prefill pipeline that exposes a decision point for microcache bypass. 2) Unit tests for each decision branch and mapping to kernel hints. 3) End-to-end e2e perf harness shows >=18% median prefill CPU reduction for short prompts (<64 tokens) on representative workloads and <=2% regression for long prompts. 4) Rollout flag and metrics in Console (prefill_path, bypass_hit, downstream_kernel_hint). 5) Code review and Security review (if flagged) completed.
notes: Design trade-offs: (a) Keep heuristic simple and deterministic to avoid adding jitter to scheduling. (b) Avoid maintaining large additional caches per-session; microcache entries must be small (fingerprint + normalized head) and evict aggressively. (c) Prefer kernel hints that favor batching when throughput is available; otherwise favor lower latency CPU paths. We may extend decision logic to learn weights from sampled telemetry in a follow-up. Rollout plan: staged by region -> customer tier -> runtime-1.22 default.
